review.alternative: Agents might be overfitting to specific parametric bounds of the proxy correlation space rather than true underlying objectives.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical evidence showing that worst-case robust formulations fail to prevent reward hacking under broader distribution shifts.

claims.statement: Formulating reward hacking as a robust policy optimization problem over the space of all r-correlated proxy rewards provides tractable max-min guarantees against proxy misspecification.

support.explanation: The paper states that formulating reward hacking over r-correlated proxy rewards yields a tractable max-min formulation protecting against worst-case proxies.
support.passage: In this work, we formulate reward hacking as a robust policy optimization problem over the space of all r-correlated proxy rewards. We derive a tractable max-min formulation, where the agent maximizes performance under the worst-case proxy consistent with the correlation constraint.

actions.findings: Formulating reward hacking as a robust policy optimization problem over the space of all r-correlated proxy rewards provides tractable max-min guarantees against proxy misspecification. [source-83f3e37ddc174b92]
actions.limitations: Max-min correlation formulations depend on specified correlation bounds and linear feature availability for full interpretability.
actions.next_questions: How do robust max-min proxy bounds scale to high-dimensional generative reward models?

actions.summary: By combining worst-case robust policy optimization over correlated proxy spaces with invariance-based stress testing, autonomous systems can better bound and mitigate reward hacking.
